(a) In General.—Section 1024(a) of the Drug-Free Communities Act of 1997 (21 U.S.C. 1524(a)) is amended—
        (1) in paragraph (9), by striking “and” after the semicolon; 
        (2) in paragraph (10), by striking the period and inserting a semicolon; and 
        (3) by adding at the end the following:“(11) $109,000,000 for fiscal year 2008;“(12) $114,000,000 for fiscal year 2009;“(13) $119,000,000 for fiscal year 2010;“(14) $124,000,000 for fiscal year 2011; and“(15) $129,000,000 for fiscal year 2012.”.  
    (b) Administration Costs.—Section 1024(b) of the Drug-Free Communities Act of 1997 (21 U.S.C. 1524(b)) is amended to read as follows:“(b) Administrative Costs.—“(1) Limitation.—Not more than 3 percent of the funds appropriated for this chapter may be used by the Office of National Drug Control Policy to pay for administrative costs associated with their responsibilities under the chapter.“(2) Designated agency.—The agency delegated to carry out this program under section 1031(d) may use up to 5 percent of the funds allocated for grants under this chapter for administrative costs associated with carrying out the program.”.

fable.w: The section only authorizes appropriation amounts for fiscal years 2008-2012 and caps the administrative costs that the Office of National Drug Control Policy and the delegated agency may charge. The tempting reading is that the name "Drug-Free Communities Act" or the reference to grants implies community involvement, but the text sets up no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue involving anyone outside the federal government. Grant funding and applications are not participation in any case.
fable.s: Not more than 3 percent of the funds appropriated for this chapter may be used by the Office of National Drug Control Policy to pay for administrative costs associated with their responsibilities under the chapter.

qwen_block.w: This section amends a statute to specify appropriation amounts and limits on administrative costs for federal agencies. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or decision-making process with parties outside the federal government. The actors mentioned are the Office of National Drug Control Policy and a designated federal agency, both of which are inside the government.
qwen_block.s: Not more than 3 percent of the funds appropriated for this chapter may be used by the Office of National Drug Control Policy to pay for administrative costs associated with their responsibilities under the chapter.

opus.w: This section only sets funding levels for fiscal years 2008 through 2012 and limits how much can go to administrative costs. It sets up no consultation, hearing, comment period, rulemaking, advisory body or right to sue that would bring outside parties into a federal decision. The mention of grants and the Act's focus on community coalitions don't change this, because the section creates no process for outsiders to take part.
opus.s: Not more than 3 percent of the funds appropriated for this chapter may be used by the Office of National Drug Control Policy to pay for administrative costs associated with their responsibilities under the chapter.
opus.b: The tempting reading is that the Drug-Free Communities Act involves community coalitions, so outside parties must be part of this. That reading fails. This section only sets funding amounts and caps on administrative costs. It doesn't consult anyone outside the government. Grants are mentioned only as a pool of money, and applying for grants doesn't count as participation anyway.
